column1: The vast expansion in international trade owes much to a revolution in the business of moving freight
column2: 国际贸易的大幅扩张，在很大程度上得益于货运业的一场变革。
column6: owes much to|在很大程度上得益于

column1: International trade is growing at a startling pace.
column2: 国际贸易正以惊人的速度增长。
column5: at a startling pace|以惊人的速度

column1: While the global economy has been expanding at a bit over 3% a year, the volume of trade has been rising at a compound annual rate of about twice that.
column2: 全球经济的年增长率略高于3%，而贸易量的年均复合增长率约为这一水平的两倍。
column7: compound annual rate|n. 年均复合增长率
column8: about twice that|约为前者的两倍

column1: Foreign products, from meat to machinery, play a more important role in almost every economy in the world, and foreign markets now tempt businesses that never much worried about sales beyond their nation’s borders.
column2: 从肉类到机械，外国产品在世界上几乎每个经济体中都比过去更重要了。过去很少关心境外销售的企业，如今也受到海外市场的吸引。
column5: play a more important role|起更重要的作用
column11: beyond their nation’s borders|在本国境外

column1: What lies behind this explosion in international commerce?
column2: 国际贸易为何会如此迅猛增长？

column1: The general worldwide decline in trade barriers, such as customs duties and import quotas, is surely one explanation.
column2: 世界各地的贸易壁垒普遍减少，例如关税降低、进口配额限制放宽，这无疑是原因之一。

column1: The economic opening of countries that have traditionally been minor players is another.
column2: 另一个原因是，一些以往在国际贸易中只占次要地位的国家开放了经济。
column5: minor players|n. 处于次要地位的参与者

column1: But one force behind the import-export boom has passed all but unnoticed: the rapidly falling cost of getting goods to market.
column2: 但促成进出口繁荣的一个因素几乎无人注意：把货物运到市场的成本正在迅速下降。
column8: falling cost|n. 不断降低的成本
column9: getting goods to market|将货物运到市场

column1: Theoretically, in the world of trade, shipping costs do not matter.
column2: 从理论上说，在贸易的世界里，运输成本无关紧要。

column1: Goods, once they have been made, are assumed to move instantly and at no cost from place to place.
column2: 理论上假定，商品一经制成，就能立即从一地运到另一地，而且不产生任何费用。
column8: from place to place|从一地到另一地

column1: The real world, however, is full of frictions.
column2: 然而在现实中，货物流通处处会遇到阻力。

column1: Cheap labour may make Chinese clothing competitive in America, but if delays in shipment tie up working capital and cause winter coats to arrive in spring, trade may lose its advantages.
column2: 低廉的劳动力成本也许能让中国服装在美国市场上有竞争力，但如果货运延误占压了流动资金，直到春天冬衣才到货，贸易的优势也可能随之消失。
column5: delays in shipment|n. 货运延误

column1: At the turn of the 20th century, agriculture and manufacturing were the two most important sectors almost everywhere, accounting for about 70% of total output in Germany, Italy and France, and 40-50% in America, Britain and Japan.
column2: 在20世纪初，农业和制造业几乎在所有地方都是最重要的两个产业。在德国、意大利和法国，两者约占总产出的70%，在美国、英国和日本则占40%至50%。
column3: At the turn of the 20th century|在20世纪之交

column1: International commerce was therefore dominated by raw materials, such as wheat, wood and iron ore, or processed commodities, such as meat and steel.
column2: 因此，国际贸易以原材料或加工商品为主。前者有小麦、木材、铁矿石，后者有肉类和钢材。

column1: But these sorts of products are heavy and bulky and the cost of transporting them relatively high.
column2: 但这类产品既重又占地方，运输成本也相对较高。

column1: Countries still trade disproportionately with their geographic neighbours.
column2: 各国的对外贸易中，与地理位置相邻的国家之间的贸易仍占有格外高的比重。
column5: geographic neighbours|n. 地理位置相邻的国家

column1: Over time, however, world output has shifted into goods whose worth is unrelated to their size and weight.
column2: 不过，随着时间推移，全球生产已转向那些价值与体积和重量无关的商品。

column1: Today, it is finished manufactured products that dominate the flow of trade, and, thanks to technological advances such as lightweight components, manufactured goods themselves have tended to become lighter and less bulky.
column2: 如今，主导贸易的是制成品。而轻型零部件等技术进步，也使制成品本身趋于更轻、更小巧。
column5: flow of trade|n. 贸易流动

column1: As a result, less transportation is required for every dollar’s worth of imports or exports.
column2: 因此，同样价值一美元的进出口货物，现在需要的运输量更小。
column6: every dollar’s worth|每一美元所对应的价值

column1: To see how this influences trade, consider the business of making disk drives for computers.
column2: 要看这种变化如何影响贸易，可以拿电脑磁盘驱动器的制造业为例。
column6: business of making|制造某种产品的行业

column1: Most of the world’s disk-drive manufacturing is concentrated in South-east Asia.
column2: 全球的硬盘制造业大多集中在东南亚。

column1: This is possible only because disk drives, while valuable, are small and light and so cost little to ship.
column2: 之所以能这样，是因为硬盘虽值钱，却体积小、重量轻，运费也就很低。
column8: cost little to ship|运输成本很低

column1: Computer manufacturers in Japan or Texas will not face hugely bigger freight bills if they import drives from Singapore rather than purchasing them on the domestic market.
column2: 日本或得克萨斯州的计算机厂商即便从新加坡进口硬盘，而不在国内市场采购，运费也不会高出多少。

column1: Distance therefore poses no obstacle to the globalisation of the disk-drive industry.
column2: 因此，距离不会妨碍硬盘制造业的全球化。

column1: This is even more true of the fast-growing information industries.
column2: 对于增长迅速的信息产业，距离更不成问题。
column3: even more true of|对……尤其如此

column1: Films and compact discs cost little to transport, even by aeroplane.
column2: 影片和光盘即使用飞机运，费用也很低。
column7: even by aeroplane|即使用飞机运

column1: Computer software can be ‘exported’ without ever loading it onto a ship, simply by transmitting it over telephone lines from one country to another, so freight rates and cargo-handling schedules become insignificant factors in deciding where to make the product.
column2: 计算机软件根本不必装船，只需通过电话线从一国传送到另一国，就可以实现“出口”。因此，决定在哪里生产软件时，货运费率和货物装卸时间安排都无足轻重。
column9: cargo-handling schedules|货物装卸时间安排

column1: Businesses can locate based on other considerations, such as the availability of labour, while worrying less about the cost of delivering their output.
column2: 企业选址可以更多地考虑劳动力是否充足等其他因素，而不必像以往那样担心把产品运出去的成本。
column6: availability of labour|n. 劳动力的可获得性

column1: In many countries deregulation has helped to drive the process along.
column2: 在许多国家，放松管制有助于推动这一进程。
column5: drive the process along|推动这一进程

column1: But, behind the scenes, a series of technological innovations known broadly as containerisation and inter-modal transportation has led to swift productivity improvements in cargo-handling.
column2: 与此同时，一系列通常统称为集装箱化与多式联运的技术革新在幕后发挥了作用，货物装卸的效率迅速提高。

column1: Forty years ago, the process of exporting or importing involved a great many stages of handling, which risked portions of the shipment being damaged or stolen along the way.
column2: 四十年前，货物进出口要经过许多道装卸、搬运环节，部分货物可能在途中损坏或遭窃。
column5: stages of handling|n. 装卸搬运环节
column7: portions of the shipment|n. 一批货物中的一部分

column1: The invention of the container crane made it possible to load and unload containers without capsizing the ship and the adoption of standard container sizes allowed almost any box to be transported on any ship.
column2: 集装箱起重机的发明使人们可以装卸集装箱而不致使船倾覆。集装箱尺寸统一后，几乎任何一个箱子都能由任何一艘船运送。
column4: container crane|n. 集装箱起重机
column8: standard container sizes|n. 统一的集装箱尺寸

column1: By 1967, dual-purpose ships, carrying loose cargo in the hold and containers on the deck, were giving way to all-container vessels that moved thousands of boxes at a time.
column2: 到1967年，舱内装散货、甲板上装集装箱的两用船，正逐渐让位于一次能运数千个集装箱的全集装箱船。
column9: were giving way to|正逐渐被……取代

column1: The shipping container transformed ocean shipping into a highly efficient, intensely competitive business.
column2: 集装箱的出现使海运业变成了一个效率很高、竞争激烈的行业。

column1: But getting the cargo to and from the dock was a different story.
column2: 但把货物运到码头或从码头运走，又是另一回事。

column1: National governments, by and large, kept a much firmer hand on truck and railroad tariffs than on charges for ocean freight.
column2: 总的来说，各国政府对公路和铁路运价的管制，过去远比对海运收费的管制严格。
column3: by and large|adv. 总的来说
column4: kept a much firmer hand on|管制得严格得多

column1: This started changing, however, in the mid-1970s, when America began to deregulate its transportation industry.
column2: 不过，到了20世纪70年代中期，美国开始放松对运输业的管制，情况也开始改变。
column4: in the mid-1970s|在20世纪70年代中期

column1: First airlines, then road hauliers and railways, were freed from restrictions on what they could carry, where they could haul it and what price they could charge.
column2: 先是航空公司，随后是公路货运企业和铁路，都摆脱了种种限制，可以自己决定运什么、运到哪里、收多少运费。
column4: road hauliers|n. 公路货运企业

column1: Big productivity gains resulted.
column2: 结果，生产率大幅提高。

column1: Between 1985 and 1996, for example, America’s freight railways dramatically reduced their employment, trackage, and their fleets of locomotives - while increasing the amount of cargo they hauled.
column2: 例如，1985年至1996年间，美国的货运铁路公司大幅减少了员工人数、运营线路总长度和机车数量，同期运送的货物却更多了。

column1: Europe’s railways have also shown marked, albeit smaller, productivity improvements.
column2: 欧洲铁路的生产率也显著提高，只是增幅较小。

column1: In America the period of huge productivity gains in transportation may be almost over, but in most countries the process still has far to go.
column2: 在美国，运输业生产率大幅提高的时期也许已接近尾声，但在大多数国家，这一进程还有很长的路要走。
column10: far to go|还有很长的路要走

column1: State ownership of railways and airlines, regulation of freight rates and toleration of anti-competitive practices, such as cargo-handling monopolies, all keep the cost of shipping unnecessarily high and deter international trade.
column2: 铁路和航空公司归国家所有，运价受到管制，货物装卸被垄断等妨碍竞争的做法也受到容忍。这些因素都使运输成本居高不下，妨碍了国际贸易。
column9: anti-competitive practices|n. 妨碍竞争的做法
column10: cargo-handling monopolies|n. 货物装卸垄断
column11: cost of shipping|n. 运输成本

column1: Bringing these barriers down would help the world’s economies grow even closer.
column2: 消除这些障碍，有助于世界各经济体之间建立更紧密的联系。
column3: Bringing these barriers down|消除这些障碍
column5: grow even closer|联系变得更加紧密
